title: adaptive-webhook-gateway-with-tenant-watermarks-and-ack-models-for-siem-integrations
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Problem: Customers sending audit streams to external SIEMs (Splunk, Datadog, generic webhooks) experience increased failure rates during load spikes and regional outages. Current forwarder offers simple retry + DLQ, but lacks tenant-scoped throttling, per-sink ordering guarantees, and a way to reconcile missed events without forcing all sinks to accept duplicate suppression headers. Goal: Build an adaptive webhook gateway that provides configurable delivery semantics per sink (at-most-once, at-least-once-with-dedupe, best-effort exactly-once via watermark reconciliation), tenant-level watermarks for ordered delivery windows, and an observable ack/backpressure model so Console can display precise SLA risk and retries. The gateway must support existing integrations (Splunk HEC, Datadog HTTP intake, generic webhooks) and integrate with RBAC v2 controls and audit logs for admin actions.
acceptance_criteria: Gateway routes audit events to configured sinks with per-sink delivery mode selectable from tenant settings
Tenant watermarking maintained: consecutive sequence watermark persisted per-sink and used to gate delivery windows
Retries follow exponential backoff and respect tenant-level throughput caps; system exposes metrics for retry queue length and oldest-unacked-age
Deduplication header accepted and validated when sink supports idempotency; when not supported gateway performs idempotent-enqueue using tenant+sequence key
DLQ behavior: persistent DLQ for events failing after max retries, with admin Console actions to requeue or export
Integration test harness for Splunk & Datadog that validates ordering and at-most-once/at-least-once semantics under failure scenarios
Security: all outbound webhooks signed using per-tenant HMAC keys; outbound credentials stored in KMS and audited
Console displays per-sink delivery health, recent failure types, and per-tenant cost impact estimates
implementation_plan: Phase 1: Design API extensions and tenant config model (watermark granularity, delivery_mode, throughput_cap). Phase 2: Build gateway service with persistent durable queue per-tenant-per-sink (Kafka topics or postgres-append + compaction) and pluggable sender adapters (splunk, datadog, generic). Phase 3: Implement watermark manager that tracks last-successful-sequence and provides leasing for ordered windows. Phase 4: Add dedupe store (Redis with TTL + idempotency keys) and optional signature header for sinks that accept it. Phase 5: Integrate with Console for controls/visibility and add metrics/tracing hooks. Phase 6: Canary rollout to subset of tenants and run chaos tests (delayed sinks, 503 loops, region partition).
design_decisions: Use hybrid delivery model: prefer at-least-once with dedupe for maximal compatibility; offer best-effort exactly-once using watermarks + one-sided reconciliation for sinks that opt-in
Durable queue implementation will use managed Kafka for high throughput; fallback single-region Postgres append log for private deployments where Kafka is unavailable
Per-tenant throughput caps enforced at gateway ingress to protect noisy neighbors
Outbound signatures will use tenant-specific HMAC keys stored in KMS; rotate keys via Console
Gateway will not hold onto PII payloads for reconciliation longer than 30 days (configurable) to meet retention/compliance policies
risks: Exactly-once semantics are hard across arbitrary third-party sinks; risk of customer confusion if guarantees differ per-sink
Watermark state introduces operational complexity and can cause head-of-line blocking for long-running sinks
Managed Kafka dependency increases ops surface for Private customers; need tested Postgres fallback
Signing keys compromise could allow forged webhooks—strong KMS/rotation and audit are mandatory
Throughput caps could unintentionally throttle bursty but valid tenant workloads if conservative defaults chosen
